title: Breaking: Every Dog Started Howling At Once
description: At 9:04 PM every dog in town howls on the same note and won't stop. Ronnie scrambles the breaking-news desk, drags in meteorologist Rhonda, and keeps upgrading the threat level as the howl resolves into, well, a setlist. Barry insists it's just dogs doing a dog thing.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: We are breaking into the regular hour on Snazzie FM. At nine oh four this evening, every dog in town began to howl. <p:0.3> Same note. All of them. We are going to rolling coverage.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, dogs howl. That's a thing dogs do.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Not on the same note, Barry. I'm classifying this as a coordinated animal event. Todd, you're at the window. Talk to me.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Yeah, hi, Ronnie. So. <p:0.3> There's about forty dogs on this block and they are all holding the exact same note. Nobody's breathing wrong. It's very clean.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's just a dog doing a dog thing. Times forty.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Forty dogs in unison is not a dog thing, Barry. We brought in a professional. Rhonda's on the weather desk. Rhonda, what are you seeing?

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: Ronnie, I want to be clear, this is not weather. I do weather. <p:0.3> But the barometer is, hang on. The barometer is keeping time. The needle is tapping. <p:0.3> Like a metronome.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: A barometer can't keep time, Rhonda.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: I know that, Barry! I have a degree! And it is currently keeping a four-four beat!

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Hello, dear. My little Pickles is sitting on the windowsill and he's leading them. <p:0.3> He raises his paw and they all come in together. He's never done choir before.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Mildred, are you telling me your dog is conducting?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: He has a little stick, dear. I don't know where he got the stick.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A baton. <p:0.3> Folks, I'm upgrading us. We are no longer a coordinated event. We are a coordinated performance.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Yeah, hi, Ronnie. So. <p:0.3> Update. The one note just became three notes. <p:0.3> They're stacked. I think the dogs are in a chord now.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: A chord is just three dogs being slightly off, Todd. That's still a dog thing.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Ronnie, I'm at Fourth and Pine, I'm pulling over because I can't drive through this. <p:0.3> Every dog at this intersection is harmonizing. I pulled into the gas station and the gas station has MORE dogs.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Darnell, do not get out of the car.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: I'm not getting out, I'm rolling the window UP, and Ronnie, they're in three-part harmony, there's a low part and a high part and a part in the middle that's frankly really good.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: Confirmed harmony, Ronnie. The radar is, hang on. <p:0.3> The radar usually shows rain. Right now it is showing measures. It drew a treble clef over the reservoir.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Radar does not draw treble clefs, Rhonda!

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: Then you come look at my radar, Barry, because mine did!

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Ronnie. <p:0.3> It's not just a chord. It's going somewhere. <p:0.3> That's a melody. <p:0.4> Oh no. I know this one.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Know what one, Todd? Name the tune.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Yeah, hi, Ronnie. So. The dogs are doing the song from the laxative commercial. <p:0.3> The whole town's dogs are howling the BurnGuard jingle.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: They have a setlist. <p:0.3> Folks, I am upgrading us again. The dogs have a setlist.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Pickles just counted them in, dear. He went one, two, one two three four. <p:0.3> With his little stick.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: A dog cannot count to four!

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: He counted to four, Barry, I heard it through the windshield!

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: They moved to the chorus! It's the cat food one now!

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: Key change! The barometer just dropped a whole step!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Upgrading!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It's DOGS, people!

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Here comes the big note!

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: They're going for the last note! <p:0.3> Every dog in town, all at once!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Hold for it. <p:0.4> Hold.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: They landed it, dear. <p:0.3> Perfect. Every single one. <p:0.3> Pickles is holding the stick up. They're holding the note.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: And, cut. <p:0.4> They stopped. <p:0.4> They're all just sitting there now. Like they're waiting.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Waiting for what?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Applause, dear. They're waiting for the applause.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: Ronnie. <p:0.3> The radar just cleared. <p:0.4> It drew one thing before it cleared. <p:0.3> It drew a cat. <p:0.4> And from every window on my block, the cats just started clearing their throats.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: We're upgrading. <p:0.3> Get me whoever books the second act.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Okay. <p:0.3> Fine. So forty dogs sang a setlist on key and took a bow. <p:0.4> I will give you the dogs, Ronnie. <p:0.3> But the cats clearing their throats? <p:0.3> That's just a cat doing a cat thing.
